name: Mizuna
grown_as: Japanese mustard greens, picked young as cut and come again or as a whole clump. William's records give no variety; green mizuna is drawn (red kinds exist).
habit: A dense fountain-like clump of many feathery leaves 20 to 30 cm tall and 30 cm across from a short stem. Bolts to 60 to 90 cm in flower.

leaf.arrangement: A crowded rosette of dozens of leaves; on the flowering stem alternate, clasping
leaf.type: Simple but deeply and finely cut (pinnately divided) almost to the midrib
leaf.outline: Long and narrow, 15 to 30 cm, cut into many narrow, jagged lobes in pairs along the midrib, the end lobe narrow; feathery overall
leaf.margin: Every lobe edged with sharp, irregular teeth, giving a fringed look
leaf.veins: A slender pale midrib, one vein into each lobe
leaf.stalk: Slender, round, crisp, white to pale green, half the leaf's length
leaf.colour: Bright mid green; stalks white. Stem leaves bluish-green, smooth, clasping with rounded ears

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.petals: Four, free, oval with a narrow claw, spreading flat
flower.centre: Six stamens, four long and two short, with yellow anthers
flower.carried: In spikes at the top of the branched bolted stem; the newly opened flowers are held above the closed buds, so the top of each spike is flat
flower.season: March to May from overwintered plants, or in summer when it bolts

fruit: Slender pods 3 to 6 cm, cylindrical with a slight bump over each seed, ending in a thin beak 1 to 2 cm, held upright-spreading on stalks along the stem. Green, drying straw-brown and splitting from the bottom to show a pale papery partition. Seeds round, 1.5 mm, red-brown to dark brown.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, broader than long with a notch at the tip, like a heart with the stalk at its point, then true leaves already toothed and soon deeply cut.
winter: Hardy: carries on as a smaller clump through a mild winter and flowers in spring.

leaf: a long narrow leaf deeply cut into many narrow, jagged lobes
a slender white stalk and midrib
bloom: four bright yellow petals in a cross
open flowers held above the closed buds
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
young: a small tuft of feathery, deeply cut leaves on white stalks
crop: a dense fountain of many feathery, finely cut leaves
white stalks gathered at the base
flower: branched stems with clasping bluish leaves
bright yellow four-petalled flowers in spikes, flat-topped
seedhead: slender beaked pods upright along the stems

look_alikes: Mibuna, its close relative, has long strap-shaped unlobed leaves. Wild rocket has deeply cut leaves but is perennial and smells strongly. Frilly mustards (Brassica juncea 'Red Frills', 'Golden Frills') are hairy and usually red or yellow-green.
